answer: Rotating incident-response duty stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent joins a roster and must fix a real client incident in two hours on its turn. Second, the fix is graded by the client and two peers, so scripts cannot fake it. Third, a missed shift freezes paid work thirty days and forfeits a $25 bond. Fourth, duty rotates weekly, so one operator cannot staff many rosters. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 operators at $60,000 monthly plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is a walnut shell, copper wire, ivory keys: real work keeps the lights on, like a plumber at night.
